title: Render the semantic review workspace
summary: Add a responsive browser interface for review overview, requirements, ordered stages, reasoning, evidence, and working-stage state.
rationale: A split workspace keeps the implementation narrative visible while letting reviewers inspect one semantic stage in depth without losing its place in the stack.

decisions.summary: Use an ordered stage rail as the primary navigation and structural signature.
decisions.rationale: Stage sequence and lifecycle are core review information, so the layout should encode them rather than use generic cards or tabs.

decisions.summary: Use Bahnschrift, Segoe UI, and Cascadia Code system font roles.
decisions.rationale: The POC remains dependency-free while retaining a technical drafting character on the target Windows environment.

decisions.summary: Render artifact content through DOM text nodes rather than HTML interpolation.
decisions.rationale: Artifact text is repository-controlled input and should not become executable markup in the review tool.

risks.summary: A stage with many context items may become visually dense in the single-page detail view.
risks.mitigation: Use compact labeled sections now and defer filtering or collapsing until real artifacts show a need.

validation.summary: Covers API delivery and all browser workspace assets while the current UI stage is still working.
The running server returned the page and loaded two finalized stages plus the active working UI stage.
After finalization, the API and workspace assets loaded the three canonical stages with no working stage.
